currentContext.expansion: The Board has approved capex of Rs 55 crore, spread over two years, to expand production capacity at the Chennai and Silvassa lubricant plants. The phased expansion is designed to lift installed lubricants capacity by about 70%, from 1,40,000 KL (240 million litres in total after expansion, versus the current combined 140 million litres) and is scheduled for commissioning in FY 2026-27. Silvassa capacity rises 55%, from 90 million litres to 140 million litres, on land acquired over the last two years; Chennai doubles from 50 million litres to 100 million litres within the existing facility. The Board describes capacity expansion as a key strategic initiative and links it to the stated ambition of 2-3x industry volume growth. Alongside the lubricants build-out, the Company strengthened manufacturing during FY 2025-26 through higher automation, SAP-enabled planning architecture, integrated manufacturing systems and automated warehousing, and invested in specialised testing infrastructure and R&D for EV driveline fluids, specialised industrial fluids and immersion cooling fluids for data centre applications. In the e-Mobility arm, Tirex capacity expansion is scheduled to commission during FY 2026-27. Property, plant and equipment rose during the year as the Company invested in its manufacturing asset base to prepare capacity for volume growth. Note: the AdBlue network comprises two in-house plants plus 12 external satellite plants.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility - base oil and additive costs tied to crude and currency
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: base oil and additive prices are influenced by global crude oil and other chemical trends and currency movements, and volatility in input costs may impact margins and pricing stability. The Directors' Report confirms this bit in FY26 - crude remained elevated through the latter part of the year, raising raw material costs and compressing margins - and management flags the Middle East crisis from March 2026 as taking input costs to multi-year high levels. Mitigation is strategic sourcing, cost optimisation, prudent inventory management and calibrated pricing actions, all of which lag the input move.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure to the INR/USD rate on imported base oils and additives
risks.note: Fluctuations in the rupee against the dollar raise the cost of imported base oils, additives and other raw materials and hit foreign-currency exposures, affecting profitability and working capital. This was a live cost in FY26: continued rupee weakness lifted input costs and drove higher foreign-exchange losses below EBITDA. Mitigation is monitoring, prudent hedging under expert advice, diversified sourcing and pricing actions.

risks.risk: Structural transition to electric mobility eroding the ICE lubricant pool
risks.note: Increasing EV adoption may gradually alter lubricant demand dynamics over the longer term, particularly in passenger vehicle segments reliant on internal combustion engines; the BRSR materiality table repeats that rising customer preference for EVs may impact demand for conventional lubricant products. The response is a calibrated hedge - expanding across the EV ecosystem through charging products and solutions and developing specialised EV fluids - which management frames as turning EVs into an additional opportunity rather than only a threat.

risks.risk: Intense competition in a fragmented, price-pressured lubricants market
risks.note: The lubricants industry remains highly competitive, with pricing pressure from established players (including public sector oil marketing companies and multinational brands), regional brands and new entrants potentially impacting market share and profitability. Counterfeit and low-quality product in the unorganised market is a related pressure on brand reputation and price. Defence rests on brand equity, distribution reach, customer engagement, premiumisation and product innovation - all reinvestment-dependent.

risks.risk: Economic and end-market cyclicality - demand tied to industrial production, auto sales and infrastructure
risks.note: Demand for lubricants is closely linked to macroeconomic indicators including industrial production, automotive sales and infrastructure activity; any slowdown in economic growth, inflationary pressure or moderation in industrial activity may impact consumption across automotive and industrial segments. Mitigation is diversification across automotive and industrial segments, a wide distribution network and rural/agricultural reach, plus continuous macro monitoring.

risks.risk: Environmental and regulatory tightening, including EPR obligations on plastics and used oils
risks.note: The industry operates under evolving environmental regulation covering emissions, waste management and product standards, and stricter norms may increase compliance requirements and operating costs. The BRSR materiality table adds that stricter emission norms for plants and lubricants may raise compliance costs, that delay in adopting energy-efficient manufacturing could reduce competitiveness, and that EPR non-compliance could bring regulatory penalties, financial implications, reputational damage and disruption to operations.

risks.risk: Technology, digital and cyber risk across an increasingly connected enterprise
risks.note: Rapid advances in manufacturing, digital systems and supply chain technology require continuous upgradation, and delays in technology adoption may impact efficiency and competitiveness. As operations move onto SAP S/4 HANA Cloud, Salesforce CRM, a data lake and partner portals, safeguarding information assets and cyber resilience become critical - managed through a governance framework, a centralised Security Operations Centre with 24x7 monitoring, and security tooling - but the dependency itself is now structural.

risks.risk: Human capital - attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent in a small permanent workforce
risks.note: The ability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent remains critical for sustaining growth and operational effectiveness; higher attrition or skill gaps may impact productivity and execution. The permanent employee base is small at 638, which concentrates execution capability in relatively few people, and mitigation rests on structured training, leadership development, engagement initiatives and workplace safety.

risks.risk: Water availability and effluent compliance at the two manufacturing sites
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications: water scarcity in operating regions may affect manufacturing continuity, and effluent discharge non-compliance could result in penalties and harm brand reputation. Because output is concentrated in only two plants (Silvassa and Chennai), a site-level water or compliance interruption is not easily absorbed elsewhere. Mitigation is Zero Liquid Discharge operations at both sites, on-site treatment and recycling, and rainwater harvesting.

risks.risk: Longer drain intervals structurally capping industry volume growth
risks.note: Management notes that technological advancement has increased lubricant life and reduced replacement frequency - beneficial for consumers but limiting volume growth for the industry. This caps the volume pool the Company is expanding capacity into, and pushes the growth burden onto share gain, premiumisation and mix rather than underlying replacement demand.

thesis (one line): Record Q4 (45,000 KL, +14% volume, 3x industry) and first-ever INR 4,000 cr+ FY26 revenue confirm GULFOILLUB's structural share-gain story (No. 2 private brand), now layered with EV-charging (Tirex INR 100 cr) and data-centre-cooling optionality — but near-term margins face a sharp crude/base-oil spike from the Middle-East crisis, with mgmt defending a 12–14% EBITDA band via repeated price hikes.

**CALL-OUT — base-oil cost:** Crude rallied from ~$65–70 (Feb) → $90+ (Mar), trending >$100 in current qtr, peaking ~$120 briefly; ~$95 "as we speak." Time-lag from crude→base-oil compressed from ~2 months to 1–2 weeks. ~50%+ base oil imported (Korea/Singapore refiners, feedstock from Middle East). Base oil inventory normally 45 days, raised to ~45–60 days for supply security; some refiners allocating at 80–90%.
**One-offs:** Some March-end demand pull-forward as customers/channel secured stock amid availability anxiety (mgmt insists Jan/Feb also double-digit, so underlying demand genuine). Rupee depreciation a headwind through FY26.
guidance (critical):
- **Volume growth:** Maintain 2–3x industry; market seen growing ~3–4% (~8–9% industry referenced by analyst). No upward revision — outlook unchanged, watching geopolitics. Target faster growth in low-share segments (PCMO <5%) and industrial (consistent double-digit). Distribution growth target 10–15% (urban + rural).
- **Margin band:** Defend **12–14% EBITDA**; aspiration to 14–16% if pricing stabilises. May trend toward lower band as realisations rise sharply (% optics). Cost levers + frequent price hikes to protect band.
- **EV / new-energy ramp:** Tirex crossed INR 100 cr in FY26; aim to grow >30% bus-DC-charger share + expand AC chargers (MG Motors, VinFast). New Tirex plant operational Q3 FY27. EV fluids into "a number of OEMs." Data-centre cooling: 2 products (PAO synthetic + mineral) developed, material-compatibility tested, next step data-centre field testing — revenue timing not yet committable; volumes small.
demand: Broad-based, robust. Double-digit growth across PCMO, motorcycle/CV, agriculture (strong), OEM franchisee workshops (40+ OEMs across auto/industrial/construction), B2B industrial. Strong FY25 vehicle sales (2W, 4W, CV, tractors; rising EV penetration; GST help) aiding OEM/workshop business. Monsoon/July agri season seen supportive. March-end aided by stock-securing behaviour but underlying demand "robust"; customers willing to pay higher prices to ensure supply.
segment (auto / industrial / ev):
- **Auto B2C (bazaar):** Good share in motorcycle & diesel-engine-oil; growing mechanic engagement & distribution. PCMO low share = growth lever.
- **OEM/franchisee workshops:** Key strength, 50–55+ OEMs, double-digit growth, leadership reinforced.
- **Industrial B2B:** Consistent double-digit, strong trajectory.
- **AdBlue:** Highest-ever volumes (40k KL qtr / 151k KL FY), +8%.
- **EV (Tirex):** INR 100 cr milestone; 30–40% share of new bus DC chargers; AC chargers to MG Motors & VinFast; new customers/OEMs testing (construction, e-truck). Indra (UK) chargers being evaluated for India. EV fluids ramping with OEMs.
growth / optionality:
- **EV charging (Tirex):** core new-energy bet; ~1 charger per 4–5 EV buses; new plant Q3 FY27; AC + DC standardized for all vehicle types.
- **Indra (UK):** global associate, leading UK AC-charger player; potential India entry.
- **Data-centre liquid-cooling fluids:** market ~14–16 mn litres (small but fast-growing as air→liquid cooling shifts); 2 products ready, in compatibility/field-test phase; "good place to be," low-volume near-term.
- **Premiumisation:** synthetic ester-based oils across categories; "Unlock 2.0" (accelerate, premiumize, transform) + digital/AI initiatives.
- **Market-share gains:** structural, low-share segments (PCMO <5%) provide headroom.
margins & cost (base oil / crude): EBITDA 12–14% band under pressure from crude spike ($65→$120 peak, ~$95 now) and rupee depreciation. ~50%+ base oil imported; crude→base-oil lag compressed to 1–2 weeks. Multiple/successive price increases taken and planned (weekly/fortnightly cadence); realisations rising sharply per-litre but with some lag in realisation. Cost recalibration levers + ~45–60 day base-oil inventory cushion margins. A&P spend ~3–4% of revenue (calibrated by quarter). Priority explicitly: supply security first, pricing second.
capex:
- **Chennai** capacity expansion on track — on stream by **Q3 FY27** (first).
- **Silvassa** expansion — by **Q4 FY27** (more civil work; started).
- **Tirex** new plant — operational **Q3 FY27**; funded via equity + borrowings + working capital.
capital allocation (high dividend): Cash-generating; debt-light. Highest-ever FY26 dividend **INR 51/share** (INR 30 final + INR 21 interim) → payout up to **~72%** (vs 30–40% three–four years ago). Payout raised pending larger M&A/EV investment opportunities. Increased Tirex stake 51%→65% (additional INR 38 cr). R&D for lubricants borne by global parent (off India P&L; large global team India-based).
risks:
- **Base-oil / crude volatility:** sharp spike + compressed lag squeezes margins; supply-chain risk if Middle-East crisis (Strait of Hormuz) prolongs — refiner allocations already at 80–90%.
- **EV-transition on ICE lubes:** long-term structural risk to engine-oil demand (mitigated offensively via Tirex/EV fluids).
- **Competition:** vs Castrol (analyst flagged GULFOILLUB operating margin ~half of Castrol's); pricing power gap closing only gradually; brand premium varies by category.
- **FX:** rupee depreciation keeps input costs elevated.
- **Pull-forward:** some March demand was stock-securing, possible Q1 normalisation.
mgmt tone: Confident, upbeat ("record quarter," "delighted"), but candid on margin/supply risk. Repeatedly stresses supply-security-over-pricing discipline and "margin management." Measured on data-centre/EV timing (refuses to commit revenue quarters). Will not comment on competitor specifics (Castrol procurement/premium).
non-obvious:
- Margin gap vs Castrol roughly 2x — closing only via volume operating leverage + brand-driven pricing power (slow).
- AdBlue is a meaningful secondary volume stream (151k KL/yr) but lower-margin commodity.
- Crude→base-oil pass-through lag collapsed to 1–2 weeks (vs historical ~2 months) — unusual, accelerates margin transmission both ways.
- EV charging tied to bus electrification, which has under-delivered ("buses expected on road have not happened") — Tirex still won 30–40% of the smaller pie.
- Brand built via cricket (MS Dhoni, Hardik Pandya, Smriti Mandhana, CSK 13+ yrs) despite global motorsports heritage — India-specific positioning.
- R&D cost largely off India P&L (parent-funded) — structural margin/return support.

**CALL-OUT — base-oil cost:** Crude rallied from ~$65–70 (Feb) → $90+ (Mar), trending >$100 in current qtr, peaking ~$120 briefly; ~$95 "as we speak." Time-lag from crude→base-oil compressed from ~2 months to 1–2 weeks. ~50%+ base oil imported (Korea/Singapore refiners, feedstock from Middle East). Base oil inventory normally 45 days, raised to ~45–60 days for supply security; some refiners allocating at 80–90%.
**One-offs:** Some March-end demand pull-forward as customers/channel secured stock amid availability anxiety (mgmt insists Jan/Feb also double-digit, so underlying demand genuine). Rupee depreciation a headwind through FY26.
guidance (critical):
- **Volume growth:** Maintain 2–3x industry; market seen growing ~3–4% (~8–9% industry referenced by analyst). No upward revision — outlook unchanged, watching geopolitics. Target faster growth in low-share segments (PCMO <5%) and industrial (consistent double-digit). Distribution growth target 10–15% (urban + rural).
- **Margin band:** Defend **12–14% EBITDA**; aspiration to 14–16% if pricing stabilises. May trend toward lower band as realisations rise sharply (% optics). Cost levers + frequent price hikes to protect band.
- **EV / new-energy ramp:** Tirex crossed INR 100 cr in FY26; aim to grow >30% bus-DC-charger share + expand AC chargers (MG Motors, VinFast). New Tirex plant operational Q3 FY27. EV fluids into "a number of OEMs." Data-centre cooling: 2 products (PAO synthetic + mineral) developed, material-compatibility tested, next step data-centre field testing — revenue timing not yet committable; volumes small.
demand: Broad-based, robust. Double-digit growth across PCMO, motorcycle/CV, agriculture (strong), OEM franchisee workshops (40+ OEMs across auto/industrial/construction), B2B industrial. Strong FY25 vehicle sales (2W, 4W, CV, tractors; rising EV penetration; GST help) aiding OEM/workshop business. Monsoon/July agri season seen supportive. March-end aided by stock-securing behaviour but underlying demand "robust"; customers willing to pay higher prices to ensure supply.
segment (auto / industrial / ev):

- **OEM/franchisee workshops:** Key strength, 50–55+ OEMs, double-digit growth, leadership reinforced.
- **Industrial B2B:** Consistent double-digit, strong trajectory.
- **AdBlue:** Highest-ever volumes (40k KL qtr / 151k KL FY), +8%.
- **EV (Tirex):** INR 100 cr milestone; 30–40% share of new bus DC chargers; AC chargers to MG Motors & VinFast; new customers/OEMs testing (construction, e-truck). Indra (UK) chargers being evaluated for India. EV fluids ramping with OEMs.
growth / optionality:
- **EV charging (Tirex):** core new-energy bet; ~1 charger per 4–5 EV buses; new plant Q3 FY27; AC + DC standardized for all vehicle types.
- **Indra (UK):** global associate, leading UK AC-charger player; potential India entry.
- **Data-centre liquid-cooling fluids:** market ~14–16 mn litres (small but fast-growing as air→liquid cooling shifts); 2 products ready, in compatibility/field-test phase; "good place to be," low-volume near-term.
- **Premiumisation:** synthetic ester-based oils across categories; "Unlock 2.0" (accelerate, premiumize, transform) + digital/AI initiatives.
- **Market-share gains:** structural, low-share segments (PCMO <5%) provide headroom.
margins & cost (base oil / crude): EBITDA 12–14% band under pressure from crude spike ($65→$120 peak, ~$95 now) and rupee depreciation. ~50%+ base oil imported; crude→base-oil lag compressed to 1–2 weeks. Multiple/successive price increases taken and planned (weekly/fortnightly cadence); realisations rising sharply per-litre but with some lag in realisation. Cost recalibration levers + ~45–60 day base-oil inventory cushion margins. A&P spend ~3–4% of revenue (calibrated by quarter). Priority explicitly: supply security first, pricing second.
capex:

capital allocation (high dividend): Cash-generating; debt-light. Highest-ever FY26 dividend **INR 51/share** (INR 30 final + INR 21 interim) → payout up to **~72%** (vs 30–40% three–four years ago). Measured on data-centre/EV timing (refuses to commit revenue quarters). Will not comment on competitor specifics (Castrol procurement/premium).

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

hero.oneLiner: Gulf Oil Lubricants India is a brand-led automotive and industrial lubricants maker with a dual-plant Silvassa-Chennai footprint, an AdBlue franchise and an emerging e-Mobility arm, growing lubricant volumes at over 3x the industry.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Gulf Oil Lubricants India is a brand-led automotive and industrial lubricants maker with a dual-plant Silvassa-Chennai footprint, an AdBlue franchise and an emerging e-Mobility arm, growing lubricant volumes at over 3x the industry.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company blends and sells automotive and industrial lubricants in India across B2C (personal mobility and commercial vehicle oils), B2B (industrial, infrastructure, mining and fleet) and OEM factory-fill and franchise-workshop channels, supported by a Chennai global R&D and Innovation Centre. It also manufactures and distributes AdBlue for BS-VI compliant vehicles through in-house plants and an external satellite network, and is building an e-Mobility business around EV charging and EV fluids. Distribution reaches retailers, organised workshops, mechanics, fleet owners and industrial key accounts across India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The domestic lubricant market is expected to keep growing at a volume CAGR of 3-4% and a value CAGR of 6-8% at least until 2033, with India among the top 3 lubricants markets globally.
- Demand supported by an expanding automotive parc, rising freight movement, increasing vehicle ownership, growth in commercial fleet operations and sustained industrial activity.
- Gradual industry shift toward higher-value, advanced and synthetic formulations, aiding mix and realisations.
- Indian GDP growth is expected to moderate to around 6.6% in FY 2026-27, with government focus on productivity, capital expenditure and trade agreements such as the India-EU FTA supporting manufacturing and industrial activity.
- Global GDP projected at around 3.0% in CY 2026 and 3.4% in CY 2027, with the outlook shaped by persistent geopolitical uncertainty and evolving trade dynamics.
- Crude volatility is the central margin variable: Brent rose from around US$69/bbl in January 2026 to briefly exceed US$100/bbl in March 2026 before moderating by end-May 2026; the evolving geopolitical environment remains very volatile and requires close monitoring.
- Rupee depreciation of nearly 9.5% against the dollar during FY26 raised import costs for energy and dollar-denominated inputs and weighed on margins in import-intensive sectors.
- Automotive end-market strength: passenger vehicles at a record ~46.43 lakh units (+7.9%), two-wheelers at a record 2.17 crore units (+10.7%), commercial vehicles at a record ~10.80 lakh units (+12.6%), and tractor domestic sales crossing 10 lakh units for the first time (+18.95%).
- Industrial demand supported by IIP growth of around 4.1% with manufacturing up around 5.0%, driven by basic metals, machinery and motor vehicles.
- Infrastructure and mining activity - high-speed corridors expanding to 5,364 km by December 2025 and captive plus commercial coal production surpassing 200 million tonnes (+10.56%) - underpins industrial and fleet lubricant demand.
- EV adoption continues to gain momentum on expanding charging infrastructure and favourable policy, which management frames as the opportunity behind the e-Mobility platform; charging infrastructure is expected to become an increasingly important part of the mobility business over time.
- Management expects the Middle East crisis from March 2026 to keep pressure on crude pricing and petroleum-product availability, taking input costs to multi-year highs.
- TIREX secured orders for bus EV chargers across multiple airports.
- TIREX continued to strengthen its leadership in the Bus OEM segment while expanding into the passenger vehicle space by onboarding new customers across dealerships, housing societies, CPOs and OEMs in both DC and AC charging solutions.
- The e-Mobility business is witnessing encouraging traction with marquee customer additions, particularly in construction and heavy commercial vehicles.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Board has approved capex of Rs 55 crore, spread over two years, to expand production capacity at the Chennai and Silvassa lubricant plants. The phased expansion is designed to lift installed lubricants capacity by about 70%, from 1,40,000 KL (240 million litres in total after expansion, versus the current combined 140 million litres) and is scheduled for commissioning in FY 2026-27. Silvassa capacity rises 55%, from 90 million litres to 140 million litres, on land acquired over the last two years; Chennai doubles from 50 million litres to 100 million litres within the existing facility. The Board describes capacity expansion as a key strategic initiative and links it to the stated ambition of 2-3x industry volume growth. Alongside the lubricants build-out, the Company strengthened manufacturing during FY 2025-26 through higher automation, SAP-enabled planning architecture, integrated manufacturing systems and automated warehousing, and invested in specialised testing infrastructure and R&D for EV driveline fluids, specialised industrial fluids and immersion cooling fluids for data centre applications. In the e-Mobility arm, Tirex capacity expansion is scheduled to commission during FY 2026-27. Property, plant and equipment rose during the year as the Company invested in its manufacturing asset base to prepare capacity for volume growth. Note: the AdBlue network comprises two in-house plants plus 12 external satellite plants.

| Bus electrification + EV penetration rising | EV DC/AC charger makers (Tirex/GULFOILLUB · 538567 · EV-charging-infra); EV-fluid suppliers | ICE-only engine-oil demand long-term | Tirex 30–40% bus-DC share, MG/VinFast AC wins; offsets ICE-lube risk ✅ |

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Record quarter — 45,000 KL (+14%, 3x industry), revenue +14%, EBITDA INR 135 cr (+8.5%, highest-ever). FY26: vol 1,68,000 KL (+10.5%), AdBlue 1,51,000 KL (+8%), revenue >INR 4,000 cr (first time), EBITDA INR 510 cr standalone / 514 cr consol. Dividend INR 51 (payout ~72%). Tirex INR 100 cr, stake →65%. Crude spike $65→$120 peak (~$95 now); 12–14% margin band defended via repeated price hikes. Chennai capex Q3 FY27 / Silvassa Q4 FY27 / Tirex plant Q3 FY27. Data-centre fluids in field-test phase.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulatory] FY26 PBT/PAT exclude an estimated Rs 22.64 crore incremental obligation from New Labour Codes; FY25 PBT/PAT excluded a one-time Rs 11.97 crore gain on sale of land & building.
- [Supply Risk] Q1 FY27 record results were achieved despite a 'West Asia supply crisis,' with management citing proactive supply-security measures to avoid customer disruption.
- [Battery Business] Gulf Pride batteries (VRLA technology; brand ambassador Hardik Pandya since 2018) hold 2-3% share of the replacement two-wheeler battery market and are among the top five players in that segment; unit sales grew from 16,000 (FY22) to 1,51,000 (FY26).
- [Industry Backdrop] India is the 3rd largest global lubricants market; industry lubricants demand is projected to grow from 2.6 to 3.6 Mn Tonnes (2023-33) at 3-4% volume / 6-8% value CAGR, driven by premiumisation, rising incomes, BS6 transition and infrastructure growth (per Kline's Global Lubricants 2023 report).
